boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Norwich rituals and customs spanning rook entry, cadet recognition, ceremonies, rings, and the university motto.

cards.title: Start with Rook Week
cards.subtitle: Corps of Cadets entry tradition
cards.notes: Learn how incoming Corps students begin as rooks during the pre-class week, then follow the official account of its basic-skills training.
cards.short_summary: The Corps’ pre-semester transition week introduces rook training and Norwich customs.
cards.evidence_claim: Norwich says Rook Week begins a week before classes and is part of rook training in basic military skills and distinctive customs.
cards.access_notes: This is a Corps of Cadets program; participation is determined by university enrollment and program requirements.

cards.title: Carry a Rock Through the Dog River Run
cards.subtitle: Rook Week culmination
cards.notes: See the official photos and description of rooks choosing a river rock, completing exercises, and carrying it along the river route.
cards.short_summary: A Rook Week culmination involving a chosen river rock and physical-training exercises.
cards.evidence_claim: Norwich identifies the Dog River Run as the culmination of Rook Week and says rooks choose and carry a river rock while completing physical training exercises.
cards.access_notes: A university-run Corps activity; do not enter the river or attempt the route outside authorized programming.

cards.title: End the Welcome with the New Student Oath
cards.subtitle: Annual ceremony for civilians and rooks
cards.notes: Read the ceremony account, which records incoming civilians and rooks pledging to uphold the Honor Code and Guiding Values.
cards.short_summary: Incoming civilian students and rooks publicly make an oath tied to Norwich values.
cards.evidence_claim: Norwich calls the Oath Ceremony a long-standing tradition in which incoming civilians and rooks promise to accept, uphold, and apply the Honor Code and Guiding Values.
cards.source_title: Scenes from the 2023 New Student Oath Ceremony
cards.access_notes: The university calendar lists this as a new-student event; attend only when included in official programming.

cards.title: Live the Rookdom Stage
cards.subtitle: Corps of Cadets first-year status
cards.notes: Use the official Corps guide to understand why new cadets are called rooks and how recognition changes that status.
cards.short_summary: The named first stage of a Norwich Corps student’s path toward becoming a cadet.
cards.evidence_claim: Norwich defines Rookdom as the first step in the Corps of Cadets and says new students are called rooks until recognized as members of the Corps.
cards.access_notes: Applies to students in the Corps of Cadets; it is not a public drop-in activity.

cards.title: Mark Recognition into the Corps
cards.subtitle: Rookdom completion ceremony
cards.notes: View the university’s Recognition coverage to see the ceremonial transition when rooks are welcomed as Corps cadets.
cards.short_summary: The formal milestone that concludes the rook period and recognizes cadets into the Corps.
cards.evidence_claim: Norwich’s official Recognition coverage describes it as welcoming the next generation of cadets and identifies Rook Recognition as the point at which rooks enter the Corps.
cards.source_title: Inspired by Tradition, Bound by Values
cards.access_notes: A Corps ceremony for eligible students and invited university participants.

cards.title: Receive the Norwich Ring as a Junior
cards.subtitle: Corps class-ring presentation
cards.notes: Explore the ring archive and ceremony description, then compare how each class documents its own crest and ring details.
cards.short_summary: The ceremony where junior Corps members receive the Norwich class ring.
cards.evidence_claim: Norwich states that the class ring is presented to junior members of the Corps at the Junior Ring Ceremony.
cards.source_title: Corps of Cadets Undergraduate Class Rings
cards.access_notes: Ring acquisition and ceremony participation are administered through Norwich; consult the university’s ring information for eligibility.

cards.title: Turn the Ring at Graduation
cards.subtitle: Corps class-ring wearing custom
cards.notes: Inspect the official ring guide for the orientation custom: the class crest faces the wearer before graduation, then the Norwich crest does.
cards.short_summary: A graduation-linked change in how Corps graduates wear their class rings.
cards.evidence_claim: Norwich says tradition directs cadets to wear the class crest facing themselves until graduation, then turn the ring so the Norwich crest faces the wearer.
cards.source_title: Corps of Cadets Undergraduate Class Rings
cards.access_notes: This custom pertains to Corps class-ring owners; a ring is required.

cards.title: Hear a Live Bugler Sound Reveille
cards.subtitle: Daily flag-honors practice
cards.notes: Read the Cadet Handbook’s ceremony section to learn why Norwich uses a bugler, rather than recorded field music, for daily calls.
cards.short_summary: Norwich’s daily Reveille practice retains live bugle calls rather than recorded field music.
cards.evidence_claim: The Norwich Cadet Handbook says it has always been Norwich custom for a bugler to sound all bugle calls and that recorded field music has not been used for these daily ceremonies.
cards.access_notes: Observe only from authorized public or campus-accessible areas and follow event staff directions.

cards.title: Observe Retreat at Day’s End
cards.subtitle: Daily national-colors ceremony
cards.notes: Consult the Cadet Handbook for the day-end flag ceremony and its sequence of bugle call, honors, and lowering of the Colors.
cards.short_summary: A daily ceremony marking the lowering of the national flag at the end of the day.
cards.evidence_claim: The Norwich Cadet Handbook describes Reveille and Retreat as daily ceremonies honoring the national flag at its raising and lowering, respectively.
cards.access_notes: Observe only from authorized public or campus-accessible areas and follow event staff directions.

cards.title: Trace the “I Will Try” Tradition
cards.subtitle: Norwich’s enduring university motto
cards.notes: Visit the Sullivan Museum’s interpretation of the 1844 flag and the competing stories surrounding the motto’s deeper history.
cards.short_summary: A campus motto with an early material record and a carefully documented origin story.
cards.evidence_claim: Norwich’s Sullivan Museum says an 1844 flag demonstrates that “I’ll Try” was in use at least three years before the often-repeated Ransom-at-Chapultepec story.
cards.source_title: Sullivan Museum and History Center Exhibitions
cards.access_notes: The museum’s exhibit page documents the flag and explains that the motto’s origin story has competing interpretations.
